$comment: The one home of villanelle's diagnostic codes. Extracted from ts/src/diagnostics.ts and ts/src/syntax/recovery.ts (MESSAGES) and py/src/villanelle/diagnostics.py and py/src/villanelle/syntax/_recovery.py (_MESSAGES) on 2026-10-28: both bindings agree on every code, constant name and message. 'layer' is the layer that owns the code: syntax (parse), written (the low level: the graph's diagnostics list them, one list for the graph, its expansion and its render, spec 6.3; the readers of an expanded value, spec 2.9, raise E4002 and E4004 to E4006), include (the include extension). 'message' is the base message (a binding may append ': <detail>'); messages are for people and are not part of the contract (spec 2.3), but generated registries use these. '{nesting depth}' is the limit of that name in api.json. 'unreadable reason' is null for a code that never makes a statement unreadable (readers raise it).

retired.now: nothing: a line break is whitespace, so a '{' may start its line (owner, 2026-10-29, Q1)
E1005, found by parse (the BAD_ESCAPE error token)

rules: Codes are stable across bindings and releases and are never reused for another meaning.
Every code is an error; there are no warning codes.
A program's own codes are '<namespace>/<name>' (api.json patterns, program code) and never collide with these.

codes.name: unterminated string
codes.meaning: A string reaches the end of its line or of the text without its closing quote.

codes.name: unexpected character
codes.meaning: A character no token may start with, or a byte-order mark after the first character.

codes.name: lone dollar
codes.message: '$' must be followed by a variable name
codes.meaning: A $ not followed by a variable name.

codes.name: bad escape
codes.meaning: A closed double-quoted string holding a backslash escape other than the six the language allows (the BAD_ESCAPE error token); placed on the whole string. A single-quoted string is raw and has no escapes (milestone 5).

codes.name: unexpected token
codes.meaning: A token the grammar does not allow here, when no more specific code applies: among them the end of the text or a '}' where a directive's ';' or block is due. Also placed in a bad text error's diagnostics by an edit's entry rule (spec 2.8): at the first token the entry rule does not allow, or at the end of the text.

codes.name: expected closing brace
codes.meaning: The text ends inside a block.

codes.name: expected closing bracket
codes.meaning: A stray ], or a [ list with no matching ].

codes.name: bad slice
codes.meaning: A malformed slice after a slice name (a word or a $name): a[~], a[1~b c], an unclosed slice, or a literal bound that is not an integer (a[x], a[1.5], a[1:3]).

codes.name: values touch
codes.message: values must be separated by a space or comment
codes.meaning: Two values with nothing between them, such as a"b".

codes.name: nesting too deep
codes.message: blocks and lists nest deeper than {nesting depth} levels
codes.meaning: Blocks and lists nested deeper than the nesting depth limit (100).

codes.name: include not found
codes.meaning: An extension's spec matched no file. Reported by the core load for every extension, despite the name.

codes.name: include resolver failed
codes.meaning: The document source rejected while resolving or reading a file an extension line names, placed at that line. Never the root file: load raises a read error for it, with no code (spec/contract.md 3).

codes.name: include bad path
codes.meaning: An @include whose values are not exactly one quoted path.

codes.name: extension failed
codes.meaning: An extension threw something other than a diagnostic error, or returned something other than a list of texts.

codes.name: unread copy
codes.meaning: An extension line's copy whose specs are not resolved or whose files are not read yet (it is in the graph's unread ()); the graph's read () reads them. Placed on the extension line's name.

codes.name: unknown extension
codes.meaning: A statement written @name where name is no language statement (set, snippet, use) and no registered extension's name (milestone 5: an extension line is written @include). Placed on the @name; the statement is an unreadable line.

codes.name: non-integer bound
codes.meaning: A slice or index bound reached through a variable ($n) whose value is not one integer word. A literal bound that is not an integer is E2007, found by parse.

codes.name: wrong value kind
codes.meaning: A reader asked for a kind the value is not.

codes.name: not a number
codes.meaning: A word read as a number that is not a JSON number, or whose value is beyond the double range (1e400, -1e400: spec/contract.md 2).

codes.name: not an integer
codes.meaning: A word read as an integer that is not one, or lies beyond plus or minus 2^53-1.

codes.name: not a boolean
codes.meaning: A word other than true or false, read as a boolean.

codes.name: bad slice name
codes.message: slice name is not one word
codes.meaning: A slice or index whose name is a $name that does not hold exactly one word ($src[0~3] with $src a string, a list or two values); placed as E4001 is for a bound through a variable.

codes.name: unknown variable
codes.meaning: A $name with no set visible and no override.

codes.name: variable set twice
codes.message: variable set twice in one block
codes.meaning: Two set lines for one name in one block.

codes.name: unknown snippet
codes.meaning: A use naming no visible snippet.

codes.name: snippet arity
codes.message: wrong number of values for the snippet
codes.meaning: A use with a different number of values than its snippet's parameters.

codes.name: snippet defined twice
codes.message: snippet defined twice in one block
codes.meaning: Two snippet lines for one name in one block.

codes.name: expansion cycle
codes.meaning: A use or extension line that reaches itself again.

codes.name: expansion too deep
codes.meaning: use and extension lines nested deeper than the expansion depth limit (16).

codes.name: too many directives
codes.meaning: More than the directives limit (100,000) after expansion.

codes.name: bad set
codes.meaning: A set line that is not @set $name value...;.

codes.name: bad snippet
codes.meaning: A malformed @snippet, or one naming a parameter twice.

codes.name: bad use
codes.meaning: A use line that is not @use name value...;.

codes.name: extension block not set
codes.message: an extension's block holds only @set lines
codes.meaning: An extension line whose block holds a line other than @set.
